verdict_summary: All six files verified ruff-formatted (ruff format --check: '6 files already formatted'), so no style discount was applied. 30 difference rows across the three units: 22 rulebook right, 7 both defensible, 1 both wrong (reason-less status-line rendering, latent and judge-unreachable), 0 native right. Native-right-zero is not reflexive rule-worship: B is a free-hand baseline that ignored the rulebook wholesale (banned `requests`, no PORT STATUS trailers, self-copied DTOs), and that showed up as four judge-catchable behavior errors — FF-3 'Bearer ' header on empty key (websearch), the invented 'Content was not found' sentinel where Go's ContentWasNotFound is '', char-length instead of byte-length thresholds, and first-title-only emission where goquery concatenates all matches (each probe-confirmed against A). The both-defensible rows are where B's instincts were behaviorally inert or the authorities were genuinely silent: param renames, guard style, selector quote characters, the decompose guard (double-decompose probed safe on bs4 4.12.3 and 4.15.0), the no-<body> branch (unreachable in Go), error-class naming, and the `input` shadowing.
